recognize_zh: 膿液抹片中可見極細、呈念珠狀（beaded）並呈直角分枝的絲狀桿菌，交織成網，這種細長分枝絲狀菌在抗酸染色下即是 Nocardia 的典型形態。
features: Very thin (about 1 micrometer) filamentous bacteria forming a loose meshwork across the field
Filaments are beaded and show branching, including near right-angle branches
Organisms stain dark purple-red against a pink-stained proteinaceous/purulent background
Filament width is much narrower than fungal hyphae, without septa or bulbous ends
Low image resolution and faded staining limit assessment of the degree of acid-fastness
describe_en: Smear of abscess drainage material stained with an acid-fast method shows a network of thin, beaded, branching filamentous bacilli lying on a pink amorphous background of proteinaceous and necrotic debris. The filaments are much narrower than fungal hyphae and show frequent branching, some at right angles. Image resolution and staining quality limit precise assessment of acid-fast intensity. Findings are consistent with Nocardia species (weakly or partially acid-fast on modified Kinyoun stain), with confirmation by culture and species identification.

ddx.vs: Actinomyces also forms thin branching filaments but is not acid-fast on modified stains and typically forms sulfur granules in anaerobic infections.
Mycobacteria are short, straight to slightly curved strongly acid-fast rods that do not branch into filaments.
Fungal hyphae are several times wider (3-6 micrometers), septate and show acute-angle or broad branching, and are highlighted by GMS or PAS rather than acid-fast stains.
